Requirement_Description: The system MUST allow a visitor to register a patient account using a person's full name, unique email address and password and MUST create the associated patient profile. Patient accounts MUST be self-registered; doctor and staff accounts MUST NOT be self-registered.
Test_Name: registers a patient, creates the profile, and persists only a bcrypt hash

Requirement_Description: The system MUST trim names, reject empty names and enforce a maximum of 120 characters. It MUST normalize email addresses consistently before uniqueness checks and reject malformed email addresses.
Test_Name: registration rejects duplicates and invalid fields with safe responses

Requirement_Description: The system MUST require a password of at least 12 characters and no more than 72 UTF-8 bytes, hash it using bcrypt before persistence, and never store or log the plaintext password.
Test_Name: registers a patient, creates the profile, and persists only a bcrypt hash | issues high-entropy HttpOnly SameSite session cookies and stores only token hashes

Requirement_Description: Patient profiles MAY include date of birth, gender and contact information. Date of birth MUST be a valid calendar date and not in the future; optional gender MUST allow a self-described value up to 80 characters and MUST NOT determine access or appointment eligibility; contact fields MUST be validated when provided.
Test_Name: patient can read and update only permitted fields on their profile | profile read and update conceal cross-account access and validate fields | beneficiary service creates minor and pending adult records and validates input | uses the injected clock and hospital-local date for calendar calculations
Notes: Profile/date/contact validation is exercised, but the inventory does not identify a test proving gender never affects access or appointment eligibility.

Requirement_Description: The system MUST authenticate patients, provisioned doctors and authorized staff and MUST derive identity and role from authenticated server-side credentials, never from untrusted client fields.
Test_Name: restores authenticated identity from the cookie and ignores client role spoofing | role denial is 403 and cannot be bypassed with client-supplied role

Requirement_Description: The system MUST provide login and logout. Successful logout MUST invalidate the current authentication context; unauthenticated access to protected operations MUST return `401 Unauthorized`.
Test_Name: logout invalidates the session and expires its cookie | expired sessions cannot restore a session or obtain a CSRF token

Requirement_Description: Login failure MUST use a generic message that does not distinguish an unknown account from an incorrect password.
Test_Name: unknown email and incorrect password return equivalent login errors | login failures use a generic message without revealing account existence

Requirement_Description: An authenticated patient MUST be able to view and update only permitted fields on their own profile. The API MUST reject updates to role, account identity or other protected ownership fields.
Test_Name: patient can read and update only permitted fields on their profile | profile read and update conceal cross-account access and validate fields

Requirement_Description: An authenticated patient MUST be able to create and manage multiple beneficiary profiles with required full name, date of birth and relationship; gender and contact information MAY be captured and MUST be validated when provided. Optional gender MUST allow a self-described value up to 80 characters and MUST NOT determine access or appointment eligibility.
Test_Name: beneficiary service creates minor and pending adult records and validates input | beneficiary HTTP endpoints create, list, read and update owner records

Requirement_Description: Each beneficiary MUST be linked to exactly one managing patient account and MUST NOT have a login account in Version 1.0.
Test_Name: authorized owner and minor can access profiles; beneficiary has no login account | enforces beneficiary ownership, approved relationships, dates and nullable authorization status

Requirement_Description: The system MUST support the relationships spouse, parent, child, sibling, other relative, legal guardian and other; when `other` is selected, a nonempty relationship description MUST be supplied.
Test_Name: beneficiary service creates minor and pending adult records and validates input | adult creation discloses only pending status and invalid input makes no changes | enforces beneficiary ownership, approved relationships, dates and nullable authorization status
Notes: Relationship input validation is tested; the inventory does not establish a separate assertion for every listed relationship value.

Requirement_Description: Among patient accounts, only the owning account may view and manage a beneficiary's profile and appointments. Doctors MAY access only relevant beneficiary details for appointments assigned to them; staff MAY access only data needed for an authorized administrative duty. For an adult beneficiary, the owning account MUST NOT manage protected details or book/view appointments until authorized hospital staff verify and approve authorization.
Test_Name: beneficiary access is isolated to the managing patient account | patient appointment list and doctor worklist expose only authorized minimal fields | staff appointment reads require view permission and minimize patient information | pending and rejected adult profiles return 422 while status remains available

Requirement_Description: Adult beneficiary creation MUST enter `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION`. The only authorization states in Version 1.0 are `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION`, `AUTHORIZED` and `REJECTED`; the only permitted transitions are `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION` to `AUTHORIZED` or `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION` to `REJECTED`. Authorized staff MUST directly confirm authorization with the adult in person or by phone before deciding and record every decision's verification method, outcome, reviewing staff identity and timestamp in preserved authorization audit history. `AUTHORIZED` and `REJECTED` are terminal states in Version 1.0; an attempted further decision MUST return `409 Conflict` with `BENEFICIARY_STATE_CONFLICT` and MUST NOT alter the state or erase/replace history.
Test_Name: authorization decisions record both outcomes and reject terminal-state retries | authorization audit history is retained after terminal-state retries | rejects updates and deletes of authorization audit records

Requirement_Description: An adult beneficiary in `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION` or `REJECTED` state MUST NOT be selectable for booking, and protected profile/appointment operations by the authenticated owning account MUST return `422 Unprocessable Content` with `BENEFICIARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`. The owner MAY read only the non-sensitive authorization status; this status read MUST NOT expose protected profile or appointment details.
Test_Name: pending and rejected adult profiles return 422 while status remains available | booking conceals cross-account recipients and rejects pending or rejected adult authorization

Requirement_Description: Every beneficiary read, update and appointment operation MUST enforce server-side role and object-level authorization. Patient operations MUST verify account ownership and adult authorization; doctor operations MUST verify assignment to the relevant appointment; staff operations MUST verify administrative permission. Client-supplied owner or relationship identifiers MUST NOT grant access.
Test_Name: authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint | beneficiary access is isolated to the managing patient account | patient appointment list and doctor worklist expose only authorized minimal fields

Requirement_Description: Staff authorization review MUST be restricted to staff with the assigned review permission; authenticated staff lacking that permission MUST receive `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN`. Each decision MUST be attributable to the authenticated staff account, recorded in preserved authorization audit history, and MUST NOT be editable by the patient who submitted the request or changed after the beneficiary reaches a terminal authorization state.
Test_Name: staff without beneficiary review permission receives 403 | authorization decisions record both outcomes and reject terminal-state retries | authorization state and audit history roll back together on audit insertion failure

Requirement_Description: Authorized staff MUST be able to provision doctor accounts with a unique work email and create doctor profiles with a full professional name, at least one specialization and one or more department associations. An approved professional description or qualification summary MAY be maintained for patient discovery.
Test_Name: staff provisions doctor account, profile and assignments without exposing credentials | doctor provisioning rejects invalid fields, duplicate email and missing assignments atomically

Requirement_Description: Doctors MUST be able to view and update only the fields of their own professional profile explicitly permitted to doctor self-management. Staff-only assignments, account role and another doctor's profile MUST be protected.
Test_Name: doctor can update only own permitted summary; private account fields and assignments stay protected | authenticated doctor self-profile route does not authorize another role

Requirement_Description: Authorized staff MUST be able to create, view and update department records and associate existing doctors with departments.
Test_Name: department HTTP supports create, view, update and duplicate conflict | department association replacement is atomic and preserves required relationships

Requirement_Description: The system MUST reject invalid doctor/department association fields with `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`, duplicate associations with `409 DUPLICATE_RESOURCE`, and references to nonexistent doctors/departments with `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, without partially persisting the operation.
Test_Name: department association replacement is atomic and preserves required relationships | department association route requires authentication and validates body fields | doctor provisioning rejects invalid fields, duplicate email and missing assignments atomically

Requirement_Description: Patient-facing doctor discovery MUST return only approved professional information, associated departments, specializations and availability; it MUST NOT return credentials, password hashes, authentication data or unrelated private information.
Test_Name: patient doctor discovery supports combined partial filters and stable bounded pagination | staff provisions doctor account, profile and assignments without exposing credentials
Notes: Discovery response minimization is cited with search/provision tests; Semgrep is a static check and is not treated as proof that no vulnerability exists.

Requirement_Description: Patients MUST be able to browse doctors and search by name or specialization; searches MUST support case-insensitive partial matching.
Test_Name: patient doctor discovery supports combined partial filters and stable bounded pagination

Requirement_Description: When both a name and specialization criterion are supplied, returned doctors MUST match both criteria. Search results MUST support bounded pagination and a stable ordering.
Test_Name: patient doctor discovery supports combined partial filters and stable bounded pagination | doctor discovery validates query shape and pagination bounds

Requirement_Description: A search with no matches MUST return `200 OK` and an empty collection; the frontend MUST show an empty-results state distinct from request failure.
Test_Name: doctor discovery validates query shape and pagination bounds | doctor discovery submits combined filters and uses stable bounded pagination

Requirement_Description: Patients MUST be able to view a selected doctor's associated department and available future slots without access to other patients' data.
Test_Name: patient doctor discovery supports combined partial filters and stable bounded pagination | booked slots cannot be modified or removed and patient schedules hide them and expose no patient data | schedule reads use stable bounded pagination and strict query validation

Requirement_Description: A doctor MUST be able to create, view and manage their own future availability slots; authorized staff MUST be able to manage availability for doctors.
Test_Name: only the doctor owner or permitted staff can manage a schedule | availability update and delete require ownership or schedule-management permission | staff schedule viewing has an independent permission from schedule management

Requirement_Description: Every availability slot MUST identify one doctor and have a valid start and end time with positive duration. The hospital MUST use one configured IANA timezone; timestamp values at API boundaries MUST be ISO 8601 date-time values with an explicit UTC offset and persisted instants MUST use UTC. Local scheduling inputs MUST be interpreted in the configured hospital timezone, and a supplied offset MUST be valid for that local date and time in that zone; nonexistent local times during a daylight-saving transition MUST be rejected, and repeated local times MUST require an explicit offset to disambiguate. “Future” is determined by comparing the slot instant with the current instant; calendar-date boundaries and adult-beneficiary age MUST use the hospital-local date. Invalid or past intervals MUST return `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`; duplicate or overlapping slots for the same doctor MUST return `409 AVAILABILITY_CONFLICT`.
Test_Name: doctor creates future availability using explicit-offset hospital-local time and persists UTC | availability rejects malformed offsets, DST gaps, past times and nonpositive intervals | converts an offset date-time only when its offset agrees with hospital timezone | rejects daylight-saving gaps and accepts repeated local times with explicit offsets

Requirement_Description: Patient availability results MUST include only configured future slots without an active `BOOKED` appointment.
Test_Name: same-doctor overlaps conflict, adjacent half-open intervals are accepted, and updates are transactional | concurrent overlapping schedule writes produce one slot and one conflict | direct SQL overlap triggers and service conflicts leave schedule unchanged

Requirement_Description: A slot associated with a `BOOKED` appointment MUST NOT be removed or changed in a way that changes its doctor or time range; such an operation MUST return `409 APPOINTMENT_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` and preserve the appointment.
Test_Name: doctor creates future availability using explicit-offset hospital-local time and persists UTC | future time on the current hospital-local date is allowed while elapsed time is rejected | repeated DST wall times require valid explicit offsets and persist as distinct instants | uses the injected clock and hospital-local date for calendar calculations

Requirement_Description: Availability MUST be revalidated as part of the booking transaction; a previously displayed slot MUST NOT be considered available solely because it appeared in an earlier response.
Test_Name: booking validates recipient shape, role, authentication, and slot availability | independent HTTP peers race on the same slot and only one booking commits | booking concurrent with cancellation is serialized and leaves no partial state

Requirement_Description: A patient MUST be able to book an appointment for self or an authorized beneficiary they manage by selecting a doctor and configured available slot. Authorized staff with appointment-booking permission MUST be able to book on behalf of a patient through the existing administrative interaction.
Test_Name: booked slots cannot be modified or removed and patient schedules hide them and expose no patient data | schedule reads use stable bounded pagination and strict query validation

Requirement_Description: Each appointment MUST identify exactly one actual recipient, the patient account responsible for the booking, and the authenticated account that initiated the operation. For patient-initiated booking, the responsible account and initiating actor are the same; for staff booking on behalf, the patient account is responsible and the authenticated staff account is recorded as actor.
Test_Name: patient books for self, minor beneficiary and authorized adult with server-attributed identity | staff booking checks patient ownership and attributes the responsible account and actor separately | rejects invalid foreign keys, slot uniqueness and CHECK constraints

Requirement_Description: A patient MUST NOT be able to book for another patient account, an unowned beneficiary or an adult beneficiary not in `AUTHORIZED` state. Staff MUST book only for a valid patient account and that account's self profile or eligible beneficiary; staff MUST NOT bypass ownership or adult-authorization rules. Cross-account resource access MUST return privacy-preserving `404 Not Found`; an authenticated owner or staff actor selecting a pending/rejected adult beneficiary MUST receive `422 Unprocessable Content` with `BENEFICIARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`. The API MUST derive initiating actor and role from authenticated identity.
Test_Name: patient books for self, minor beneficiary and authorized adult with server-attributed identity | booking conceals cross-account recipients and rejects pending or rejected adult authorization | booking validates recipient shape, role, authentication, and slot availability

Requirement_Description: The system MUST prevent a doctor from having overlapping active `BOOKED` appointments, including bookings against distinct but overlapping availability slots. Patient- and staff-initiated booking MUST atomically recheck interval availability and commit no more than one active appointment for overlapping time for a doctor, including under concurrent requests. A booking racing with cancellation MUST be serialized: if booking is processed before cancellation commits, it returns `409 APPOINTMENT_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`; if cancellation commits first, a subsequent booking MAY succeed only if the slot interval is still future and available. Losing booking requests MUST NOT be retried automatically.
Test_Name: independent HTTP peers race on the same slot and only one booking commits | active interval conflicts reject bookings even when overlapping slots predate integrity triggers | booking concurrent with cancellation is serialized and leaves no partial state | competing cancellation and completion have exactly one winner

Requirement_Description: Appointment statuses MUST be `BOOKED`, `CANCELLED` or `COMPLETED`. A `BOOKED` appointment MAY transition to `CANCELLED` or `COMPLETED`; `CANCELLED` and `COMPLETED` are terminal in Version 1.0.
Test_Name: patients can cancel owned bookings; assigned doctors complete and terminal transitions conflict | assigned doctor sees and completes worklist; staff view has no complete or reschedule actions

Requirement_Description: A patient MAY cancel a `BOOKED` appointment for self or an authorized beneficiary they manage. Authorized staff with appointment-cancellation permission MAY cancel a `BOOKED` appointment. Only the assigned doctor MAY mark it `COMPLETED`; no other role may perform these transitions. Staff MUST NOT directly reschedule an existing appointment, change its doctor or time slot as an update to that appointment, or mark it `COMPLETED`. An invalid transition MUST return `409 Conflict` with `APPOINTMENT_STATE_CONFLICT`.
Test_Name: patients can cancel owned bookings; assigned doctors complete and terminal transitions conflict | permission-scoped staff cancellation and cancellation releases only a future slot | patient booking and cancellation remain unconfirmed until the server responds

Requirement_Description: Cancellation MUST be transactional, set status to `CANCELLED` and release the corresponding slot for future booking only if its interval is still future and available. Completed or cancelled appointments MUST NOT occupy an active slot; completion does not make an elapsed slot bookable again. Concurrent cancellation and assigned-doctor completion of the same `BOOKED` appointment MUST be serialized so exactly one transition commits and the losing request returns `409 APPOINTMENT_STATE_CONFLICT`.
Test_Name: patients can cancel owned bookings; assigned doctors complete and terminal transitions conflict | competing cancellation and completion have exactly one winner | assigned doctor sees and completes worklist; staff view has no complete or reschedule actions

Requirement_Description: Patients MUST be able to view upcoming and historical appointments for self and authorized beneficiaries. Doctors MUST be able to view upcoming appointments assigned to them and relevant associated patient details. Authorized staff with appointment-view permission MUST be able to view appointments and doctor schedules/availability within their administrative permissions.
Test_Name: patient appointment list and doctor worklist expose only authorized minimal fields | patient history excludes pending adults and includes terminal and elapsed appointments | staff appointment reads require view permission and minimize patient information

Requirement_Description: Every appointment read, creation, status update and cancellation MUST enforce role and object-level authorization on the backend. Patient access MUST verify account ownership and, for adult beneficiaries, authorization; doctor access MUST verify assignment to the appointment; staff access MUST verify the permission for the operation, and staff booking on behalf MUST verify the responsible patient account owns the selected recipient and has adult-beneficiary authorization. Unauthenticated requests MUST return `401`; authenticated callers lacking a required role/permission MUST return `403`; cross-account or unassigned object access MUST return privacy-preserving `404`. An authenticated owning patient or staff member with booking permission who attempts booking for a pending/rejected adult beneficiary MUST receive `422` with `BENEFICIARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`. Unauthorized access MUST NOT reveal protected patient details.
Test_Name: authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint | patient appointment list and doctor worklist expose only authorized minimal fields | booking conceals cross-account recipients and rejects pending or rejected adult authorization | staff appointment reads require view permission and minimize patient information

Requirement_Description: Patient- or staff-initiated booking, cancellation and permitted doctor status changes MUST use database transactions or equivalent atomic operations so failures cannot leave appointment status and slot availability inconsistent or permit duplicate/overlapping active bookings. Staff-created appointments MUST record the actual recipient, responsible patient account and authenticated staff actor.
Test_Name: failed appointment persistence rolls back the booking transaction | independent HTTP peers race on the same slot and only one booking commits | booking concurrent with cancellation is serialized and leaves no partial state | competing cancellation and completion have exactly one winner
Notes: Booking rollback and concurrency/transition races are tested; the inventory does not identify a cancellation fault-injection test proving rollback leaves both status and slot unchanged.

Requirement_Description: The administrative dashboard MUST be available only to authenticated staff with appropriate permissions and MUST provide access to registered patients, doctors, departments, appointments, doctor availability and pending adult-beneficiary authorization reviews.
Test_Name: admin dashboard and patient directory are permission-scoped with empty-list behavior | staff dashboard provisions doctors and makes patient directory reads permission-scoped

Requirement_Description: Staff MUST be able to view registered patients, but patient and beneficiary fields returned MUST be limited to information necessary for the authorized administrative operation.
Test_Name: staff appointment reads require view permission and minimize patient information | admin dashboard and patient directory are permission-scoped with empty-list behavior

Requirement_Description: Version 1.0 administrative views MUST NOT introduce unrelated analytics or reporting capabilities.
Test_Name: admin dashboard and patient directory are permission-scoped with empty-list behavior

Requirement_Description: Every protected API MUST authenticate and authorize each operation independently of frontend route protection.
Test_Name: authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint | role denial is 403 and cannot be bypassed with client-supplied role

Requirement_Description: Body-bearing API responses MUST follow the success or error envelope, status semantics and stable error codes defined in API Contract. `204 No Content` MUST have no response body.
Test_Name: 204 success has no body and body-bearing success uses the approved envelope | returns stable duplicate, unauthorized and privacy-safe not-found errors | central response helper emits the standard 204 response

Requirement_Description: Malformed request structure MUST return `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; validly structured field/domain validation failures MUST return `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`; missing/invalid authentication MUST return `401`; missing role/permission MUST return `403 FORBIDDEN`; privacy-sensitive cross-account access MUST return `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; pending/rejected adult-beneficiary eligibility MUST return `422 BENEFICIARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`; and slot/state conflicts MUST return `409` with the applicable stable code. Validation errors MUST return field-level details where applicable. Error responses MUST NOT expose stack traces, SQL, database errors, credentials or internal implementation details.
Test_Name: maps malformed structure to 400 and validly structured field errors to 422 | returns stable duplicate, unauthorized and privacy-safe not-found errors | authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint | booking conceals cross-account recipients and rejects pending or rejected adult authorization

Requirement_Description: The frontend MUST display clear success, validation, authentication, authorization, not-found, conflict, empty-result, network and unexpected-error feedback using the User Feedback requirements.
Test_Name: API client returns only safe mapped errors and rejects malformed envelopes | patient registration shows validation/network feedback and explicit success before sign-in | beneficiary listing hides pending adult identity and supports an authorized minor update | doctor discovery submits combined filters and uses stable bounded pagination | patient booking and cancellation remain unconfirmed until the server responds

Requirement_Description: The frontend MUST show loading feedback for pending requests and ask for confirmation before appointment cancellation. It MUST NOT display a booking or cancellation as successful before the server confirms the operation.
Test_Name: patient registration shows validation/network feedback and explicit success before sign-in | patient booking and cancellation remain unconfirmed until the server responds | API client returns only safe mapped errors and rejects malformed envelopes

Requirement_Description: When an operation fails due to a network, conflict or server error, the frontend MUST preserve the last server-confirmed state and clearly state that the action was not confirmed.
Test_Name: patient booking and cancellation remain unconfirmed until the server responds | patient login, profile saving and sign-out show only confirmed outcomes | adult beneficiary creation shows safe validation/network feedback and only confirmed status

Requirement_Description: **Given** a visitor provides a valid name, unique email address and password, **When** they submit registration, **Then** the system creates one patient account, stores no plaintext password, returns `201 Created`, and does not create a doctor or staff account.
Test_Name: registers a patient, creates the profile, and persists only a bcrypt hash

Requirement_Description: **Given** the email address is already registered, **When** a visitor submits registration using that address, **Then** no duplicate account is created and the API returns `409 Conflict` with `DUPLICATE_RESOURCE`.
Test_Name: registration rejects duplicates and invalid fields with safe responses

Requirement_Description: **Given** a patient submits malformed JSON or omits required request structure, **When** registration is attempted, **Then** the system returns `400 Bad Request` with `INVALID_REQUEST`; given a structurally valid request with invalid field values, **Then** it returns `422 Unprocessable Content` with `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Both responses identify invalid fields without echoing secrets and create no account.
Test_Name: registration rejects duplicates and invalid fields with safe responses | maps malformed structure to 400 and validly structured field errors to 422

Requirement_Description: **Given** a registered patient provides the correct email and password, **When** they log in, **Then** the system establishes an authenticated patient context and returns `200 OK`.
Test_Name: issues high-entropy HttpOnly SameSite session cookies and stores only token hashes | patient login, profile saving and sign-out show only confirmed outcomes

Requirement_Description: **Given** an unknown email or incorrect password, **When** login is attempted, **Then** the system returns `401 Unauthorized` with `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` and the same generic message for both cases, revealing no account-existence information.
Test_Name: unknown email and incorrect password return equivalent login errors | login failures use a generic message without revealing account existence

Requirement_Description: **Given** a patient is authenticated, **When** they update permitted fields on their own profile, **Then** only those fields change and the response contains the updated permitted profile data.
Test_Name: patient can read and update only permitted fields on their profile | patient login, profile saving and sign-out show only confirmed outcomes

Requirement_Description: **Given** a patient attempts to read or update another patient's profile by changing an identifier, **When** the request reaches the API, **Then** it returns privacy-preserving `404 Not Found` with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` and the other profile remains unchanged.
Test_Name: profile read and update conceal cross-account access and validate fields

Requirement_Description: **Given** a patient is authenticated, **When** they log out, **Then** their authentication context is invalidated and subsequent protected requests using it return `401 Unauthorized` with `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`.
Test_Name: logout invalidates the session and expires its cookie | patient login, profile saving and sign-out show only confirmed outcomes

Requirement_Description: **Given** an authenticated patient submits a valid beneficiary profile with name, date of birth and relationship, plus optional gender and any applicable contact details, **When** the beneficiary is a minor, **Then** the beneficiary is linked to that account, has no login account, and the owner can view and update the beneficiary profile.
Test_Name: beneficiary HTTP endpoints create, list, read and update owner records | authorized owner and minor can access profiles; beneficiary has no login account

Requirement_Description: **Given** an authenticated patient submits a beneficiary who is an adult, **When** the request is received, **Then** the beneficiary is created in `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION` state with `201 Created`; subsequent protected profile or appointment operations by that owner return `422 Unprocessable Content` with `BENEFICIARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED` until authorized hospital staff verify and approve authorization.
Test_Name: adult creation discloses only pending status and invalid input makes no changes | pending and rejected adult profiles return 422 while status remains available

Requirement_Description: **Given** an adult beneficiary authorization request is `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION`, **When** authorized staff directly confirm the adult's authorization in person or by phone and approve or reject it, **Then** the only permitted transitions are to `AUTHORIZED` or `REJECTED`, respectively, and each decision is recorded in the preserved authorization audit history with verification method, outcome, reviewing staff identity and timestamp. An authenticated staff actor without review permission receives `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN`.
Test_Name: authorization decisions record both outcomes and reject terminal-state retries | staff without beneficiary review permission receives 403

Requirement_Description: **Given** an adult beneficiary is already `AUTHORIZED` or `REJECTED`, **When** staff attempt another authorization decision, **Then** the API returns `409 Conflict` with `BENEFICIARY_STATE_CONFLICT`, leaves the state unchanged and does not replace or erase the existing audit history.
Test_Name: authorization decisions record both outcomes and reject terminal-state retries | authorization audit history is retained after terminal-state retries

Requirement_Description: **Given** an adult beneficiary is `AUTHORIZED`, **When** the owning patient views, updates or selects the beneficiary, **Then** access is permitted only for that authenticated owner account and permitted fields.
Test_Name: authorized owner and minor can access profiles; beneficiary has no login account | beneficiary access is isolated to the managing patient account

Requirement_Description: **Given** an authenticated owning patient attempts a permitted profile or booking operation for an adult beneficiary whose authorization is pending or rejected, **When** the request is processed, **Then** the API returns `422 Unprocessable Content` with `BENEFICIARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, does not disclose protected details beyond the owner's non-sensitive authorization status, and makes no change.
Test_Name: pending and rejected adult profiles return 422 while status remains available | booking conceals cross-account recipients and rejects pending or rejected adult authorization

Requirement_Description: **Given** a patient attempts to read or modify a beneficiary or appointment owned by another account by supplying its identifier, **When** the request is processed, **Then** the API returns privacy-preserving `404 Not Found` with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` and makes no changes.
Test_Name: beneficiary access is isolated to the managing patient account | booking conceals cross-account recipients and rejects pending or rejected adult authorization

Requirement_Description: **Given** an account submits malformed beneficiary request structure, **When** the request is processed, **Then** the API returns `400 Bad Request` with `INVALID_REQUEST`; given a structurally valid request with invalid fields, unsupported relationship or invalid/future date of birth, **Then** it returns `422 Unprocessable Content` with `VALIDATION_FAILED` and safe field-level details, and persists no invalid change.
Test_Name: beneficiary service creates minor and pending adult records and validates input | adult creation discloses only pending status and invalid input makes no changes

Requirement_Description: **Given** a beneficiary record is updated, **When** the update is saved, **Then** its owning account and authorization state cannot be reassigned by client-supplied identifiers; a patient attempting a staff-only authorization change receives `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN`, and no change is made.
Test_Name: adult creation discloses only pending status and invalid input makes no changes | patient can read and update only permitted fields on their profile

Requirement_Description: **Given** an unauthenticated caller attempts a protected beneficiary operation, **When** the API receives the request, **Then** it returns `401 Unauthorized` with `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`; given an authenticated role without permission for the operation, **Then** it returns `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN`, unless the request is cross-account object access that must be concealed with `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
Test_Name: authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint | staff without beneficiary review permission receives 403

Requirement_Description: **Given** an authenticated staff user with doctor-management permission submits valid required doctor details, **When** they create a doctor, **Then** the system creates a provisioned doctor account and professional profile and returns `201 Created`.
Test_Name: staff provisions doctor account, profile and assignments without exposing credentials

Requirement_Description: **Given** a patient or doctor attempts an operation requiring staff role, **When** the request is made, **Then** it returns `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN`; given an unauthenticated caller, **Then** it returns `401 Unauthorized` with `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`. No record changes.
Test_Name: patients, doctors and unpermitted staff cannot provision doctors | authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint

Requirement_Description: **Given** a doctor is authenticated, **When** they update fields they are authorized to manage on their own professional profile, **Then** only those fields are updated; an attempt to change account role, department assignment or staff-controlled fields returns `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN` and makes no change.
Test_Name: doctor can update only own permitted summary; private account fields and assignments stay protected

Requirement_Description: **Given** required doctor details reference a nonexistent department, **When** staff submit the profile, **Then** the API returns `404 Not Found` with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; given a structurally valid profile with invalid field values, **Then** it returns `422 Unprocessable Content` with `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Neither case creates a partial doctor record.
Test_Name: doctor provisioning rejects invalid fields, duplicate email and missing assignments atomically | department association route requires authentication and validates body fields

Requirement_Description: **Given** a doctor profile is returned in patient discovery, **When** a patient views it, **Then** only approved professional information, specialization, department and availability are disclosed; staff credentials and unrelated private information are omitted.
Test_Name: patient doctor discovery supports combined partial filters and stable bounded pagination | staff provisions doctor account, profile and assignments without exposing credentials

Requirement_Description: **Given** authorized staff submits a valid department name and description, **When** they create a department, **Then** the system returns `201 Created` with the new department.
Test_Name: department HTTP supports create, view, update and duplicate conflict

Requirement_Description: **Given** an authorized staff user updates a department or assigns an existing doctor, **When** the change is valid, **Then** the directory reflects the update and the doctor-department relationship is preserved.
Test_Name: department association replacement is atomic and preserves required relationships

Requirement_Description: **Given** an attempted duplicate department name, **When** staff submit the operation, **Then** the API returns `409 Conflict` with `DUPLICATE_RESOURCE`; given an association to a nonexistent doctor or department, **Then** it returns `404 Not Found` with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Existing relationships remain unchanged.
Test_Name: department HTTP supports create, view, update and duplicate conflict | department association replacement is atomic and preserves required relationships

Requirement_Description: **Given** an authenticated patient or doctor attempts to create, update or assign departments, **When** the request is made, **Then** the API returns `403 Forbidden` with `FORBIDDEN` and makes no change; an unauthenticated caller receives `401 Unauthorized` with `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`.
Test_Name: patient, doctor and unpermitted staff cannot administer departments | authorization matrix requires authentication on every protected API endpoint

Requirement_Description: **Given** a department has associated doctors, **When** staff attempt to remove or invalidate an association that is required by existing data, **Then** the system returns `409 Conflict` with `RESOURCE_IN_USE` and preserves referential integrity.

Requirement_Description: **Given** doctors have active, discoverable profiles, **When** a patient browses the doctor directory, **Then** the system returns doctor profiles with their department and specialization and does not expose private account data.

Requirement_Description: Run the benchmark against a local HMS instance and a fresh SQLite test database populated with fictional data by a deterministic, version-controlled fixture generator using the fixed seed `20261107`. The fixture MUST contain 200 patient accounts, 100 beneficiaries (including minors and adults in pending, authorized and rejected states), 20 doctors, 10 departments, 300 future availability slots and 500 appointments across all three statuses, with relationships and conflicts valid under this specification. It MUST include at least 100 unbooked future slots for booking samples and at least 100 distinct future `BOOKED` appointments for cancellation samples. Use 3 concurrent local clients and exclude application startup and fixture generation/reset from measurements. For each endpoint, create a fresh database from the same fixture; run 10 warm-up requests, then for mutating endpoints discard that database and restore the same fixture before collecting at least 100 successful measured samples. Use distinct preconditioned slots/appointments for each write sample. Paginated reads MUST use page size 20 and stable sorting; doctor search MUST use the same fixture-defined query with a fixed non-empty result set for warm-ups and measured samples. Use the same authenticated actors and request parameters throughout a run. Run requests in deterministic batches of at most 3 concurrent clients; do not automatically retry failed requests. Measure client-observed request duration, excluding reset/seed time. Compute p95 using the nearest-rank method (sort the measured durations and select the value at rank `ceil(0.95 * n)`, with ranks starting at 1). The p95 MUST be at most 1,000 ms for search and paginated reads and at most 2,000 ms for booking and cancellation; all measured samples MUST succeed or the operation fails acceptance. Record the fixture seed, generator revision and fixture-manifest hash, counts by entity and relevant state/workflow cohort, endpoint and operation, search query and expected result count, page size and sort order, hardware/OS/runtime versions, database setup, concurrency, batch order, warm-up and sample counts, elapsed-time distribution including p95, failures and pass/fail for each operation. This is a reproducible local Version 1.0 acceptance benchmark only; it is not a production capacity or scalability claim.
Test_Name: fixture manifest, fixed clock and entity cohorts match the approved dataset | benchmark protocol fixes warm-ups, measured count, page size and concurrency | reset and setup time are excluded from measured request durations | booking and cancellation measurements use distinct future fixture targets | independent benchmark records all samples, warm-ups, concurrency and sanitized outcomes
Notes: T053 retained results record five operations, 10 warmups and 100 measured samples each, zero measured failures, and passing nearest-rank p95 thresholds.
